conviction_note: The bar (about $0.54 operating EPS) sits about $0.29 below the $0.83 RLI printed in each of the last three quarters, which embeds a seasonal hurricane load. Q3 2026 had the quietest North Atlantic on record (no hurricane until Isaias on Oct 9) and RLI filed no cat pre-announcement, so a beat is likely (my point estimate is about $0.68, +25%). Three Hawaii hurricanes, softening E&S property, an 8.4% five-day run-up into the print and the sector selling Travelers' beat keep the reaction lean small: p_up 57 on abs 4.0 gives +0.56, against a findings sum of +0.5. The two measurements agree.
bar: Q3 2026 operating EPS consensus about $0.54. Sources: MarketBeat $0.514 on $533.5M revenue (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/upcoming-rli-rli-projected-to-release-earnings-on-monday-2026-10-12/, 2026-10-12); Earnings Whispers and Barchart $0.54 (https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/RLI, https://www.barchart.com/story/news/3392231/rli-s-earnings-decline-might-actually-signal-underwriting-discipline-returning). The sweep row carries $0.58 without a source. Two estimate sources agree within 3 cents, so findings are not capped. The bar compares with operating EPS of $0.83 in Q3 2025, Q1 2026 and Q2 2026 (Q2 2026 release: https://s204.q4cdn.com/949661285/files/doc_news/RLI-Reports-Second-Quarter-2026-Results-2026.pdf). RLI gives no guidance.
positioning_check: Short interest 8,807,160 shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement, about 9.6% of 91.77M shares outstanding, days to cover 10.84. That is up from 7.65M on 2026-07-15 and peaked at 16.4 DTC on 09-15 (https://equibles.com/stocks/rli/short-interest). Swingtradebot shows 10.4% of float and 12.7 DTC, undated (https://swingtradebot.com/equities/RLI). This is a crowded short for an A++ specialty insurer. Sell side leans bearish: MarketBeat consensus 'Reduce', target $63.20; Jefferies Underperform $53 since 2026-08-25. No usable option chain: ATM legs not two-sided, skew null, total OI 386, so the option market says nothing. The tape shows +8.37% over 5 days and +3.89% over 20 days, spot 61.37, 7.9% below the 52-week high, with gap-ups on Oct 15 (+2.1%), Oct 16 (+2.7%) and the Oct 19 open (+1.7%). That may be short covering ahead of a benign-cat print.

findings.finding: Q3 2026 had no Atlantic hurricane at all. Moody's (2026-09-22) records the latest first hurricane of the satellite era and ACE 93% below normal; the first hurricane, Isaias, made landfall on Oct 9, in Q4. RLI's largest cat exposure, Gulf and East Coast commercial property, was untouched. The ~$0.54 bar is ~$0.29 below the $0.83 run-rate of the last three quarters, about $35M pretax, which is the size of a typical RLI hurricane quarter (Beryl/Helene 2024 cost $35-40M).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 was the same setup (benign hurricane season, minimal cats). Operating EPS $0.83 beat Zacks consensus by 33.9% and the stock moved +2.78%. Q2 2026's beat ($0.83 vs $0.72) got +3.68%; Q1 2026's beat ($0.83 vs $0.78) got -3.80%.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus has not moved off its seasonal cat load: estimates of about $0.54-0.57 date back to March (Zacks $0.57 on 2026-03-23), and AAII (Oct 19) shows 1 of 8 analysts cutting next-quarter EPS last month and none raising. If the quiet season were in the number, consensus would sit near the $0.75-0.83 run-rate. The 8.4% five-day run-up suggests the tape has partly priced it, hence the modest size.
findings.independence: Verisk via insurance-edge (2026-10-15) says Isaias was the season's first hurricane, ninth named storm, landfall Oct 9: https://insurance-edge.net/2026/10/15/verisk-estimates-hurricane-isaias-losses-in-the-1bn-2bn-range/. RLI's Q3 2025 release credits 'minimal catastrophe activity' for an 85.1 combined ratio: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/84246/000110465925100820/rli-20251020xex99d1.htm. This is a weather proxy; the company has not confirmed it.

findings.finding: Three Hawaii hurricanes hit RLI's Hawaii homeowners book in Q3: Lala (mid-August, Big Island, mostly flood), Lowell (passed west of Niihau Sept 7 as a Cat 2; Kauai hardest hit; Cotality insured estimate $0.5-1.0B) and Nolo (late September). RLI's 10-K names Hawaii homes as part of its second-largest cat exposure. In 2023 it took up to $75M net from the $3.2B+ Maui wildfire, about 2% of industry loss, which at Lowell's size implies roughly $10-20M before reinsurance.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2023, with the Maui wildfire loss pre-announced in August, is not in the baseline window. The Q1 2025 print (fell -3.65%) carried LA wildfire cats. Cat-heavy prints have been sold more than light ones have been bought.
findings.why_not_priced: Hawaii storms get little coverage from Gulf-focused insurance analysts, and no aggregator ties them to RLI. Consensus did not move after Lowell (AAII: current-year estimates up 1.2% last month). If the market were worried, the stock would not have run +8.4% into the print.
findings.independence: Moody's 2026-09-22 (same document as finding 1) describes Lala and Lowell damage: 10 homes destroyed and 64 with major damage on Kauai. Maui precedent: https://intelligentinsurer.com/news/rli-pegs-up-to-75m-hit-from-hawaii-homeowners-wildfire-losses-33352 (2023-08-24). Exposure statement: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000084246/000110465907032273/a07-10993_110q.htm (2007, dated). Finding 3 bounds this one's size.

findings.finding: RLI filed no catastrophe pre-announcement for Q3 2026. EDGAR shows only a dividend 8-K (Aug 13) and Form 4 grants between the Jul 28 8-K and Oct 19. RLI did pre-announce Q3 cat losses in prior heavy quarters: Beryl/Helene $35-40M on 2024-10-07, two weeks before the print; Maui up to $75M on 2023-08-24; Ian, Ida. That points to Q3 2026 cats, Hawaii included, landing below the ~$35M scale the company flags, which is roughly the gap the bar embeds.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Same line as finding 1. Q3 2025, with no pre-announcement and light cats, went +2.78% on a 34% beat.
findings.why_not_priced: An absence of filings is not on any wire. Analysts holding a $0.54 bar are implicitly carrying a loss the company would normally have flagged by now.
findings.independence: Precedent release: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20241007586136/en/RLI-Announces-Hurricane-Beryl-and-Hurricane-Helene-Loss-Estimates (2024-10-07). This is an inference from a disclosure pattern, not a company number. It bears on the same quantity (Q3 cat losses) as findings 1 and 2.

findings.finding: Property top line is shrinking as E&S property prices fall. Q2 2026 property gross premiums written were $199.3M against $211.8M (-5.9%), surety -5.5%, casualty +10.6%, total +3%. E&S property rates are reported down 15% to 30-40% in places. Q3 property GWP likely falls further, and the call (Oct 20) will be asked about the property margin outlook. Net of casualty growth, total premium growth stays in low single digits.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 (GWP +3%, property down) went -3.80% despite an EPS beat. Q2 2026 (GWP +3%, casualty-led) went +3.68%.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: Jefferies' Underperform and the 'Reduce' consensus cite property margin pressure. It is filed because the size of the Q3 property decline is not yet known and the stock has run up into it.
findings.independence: TD Cowen via Reinsurance News: E&S growth slows as property pricing weakens, https://www.reinsurancene.ws/es-insurance-growth-slows-as-property-pricing-weakens-in-may-2026-update-td-cowen/. Risk & Insurance: https://riskandinsurance.com/es-property-market-shifts-buying-power-to-insureds-in-2026/.

findings.finding: Casualty margins are thin and are the bear case's focus. The Q2 2026 casualty combined ratio was 99.3 against 96.5 a year earlier, underwriting income $1.7M on $257M earned, even with $13.7M of favorable casualty prior-year development. Jefferies (Aug 25) put 2026-28 EPS ~7% below consensus on higher modeled casualty accident-year loss ratios. A casualty loss-pick increase or adverse development in Q3 would land on the line the shorts are watching.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The baseline does not separate it out. The Q2 2026 print, with casualty at 99.3, was still bought (+3.68%) on the headline beat.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced through the 9.6% short interest and the Jefferies call. What is unpriced is whether Q3 shows the casualty ratio crossing 100, which would be visible on the release line.
findings.independence: Jefferies downgrade via StockStory: https://investor.wedbush.com/wedbush/article/stockstory-2026-8-25-why-rli-rli-stock-is-down-today (2026-08-25). It shares the Q2 release with finding 4.

findings.finding: Short interest has built steadily into the print: 8.81M shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement (about 9.6% of shares outstanding, 10.8 days to cover), up from 7.65M on 07-15, with DTC peaking at 16.4 on 09-15. That is crowded for a low-volatility A++ insurer, and a cat-light beat gives the shorts a reason to cover in the first session.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None in the baseline. The Oct 15-19 gap-ups (+2.1%, +2.7%, +1.7%) look like covering has already begun, which cuts both ways.
findings.why_not_priced: Short interest is public, but the squeeze depends on the print. The 8.4% run-up suggests part of the covering already happened before the event, so it is sized below its range high.
findings.independence: Swingtradebot: 10.4% of float, 12.7 DTC, https://swingtradebot.com/equities/RLI. Sell-side bearishness (Reduce consensus, Jefferies $53) explains why the short is there: https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/upcoming-rli-rli-projected-to-release-earnings-on-monday-2026-10-12/.

findings.finding: The sector sold its first big Q3 beat. Travelers (Oct 16) reported adjusted EPS $9.18 against $7.25 expected, record investment income and more favorable development, and fell ~4.4% premarket on higher cat losses ($538M, from wind and hail) and a $295M asbestos charge. Insurance holders are not paying up for beats driven by reserves and cats this season.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Peer read; no RLI history. RLI itself rose +2.67% on Oct 16, the day Travelers fell.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a reaction-function datum, not a fact about RLI. RLI's rise the same day shows the market separated the two names, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: Travelers 10-Q: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000086312/000008631226000181/trv-20260930.htm. Travelers is personal and commercial lines with SCS exposure, unlike RLI's E&S book, so the read-across is weak.

findings.finding: Investment income keeps compounding. Q2 2026 net investment income rose 17% to $46.0M, with portfolio total return 3.4% and invested assets $4.87B. The $184M special dividend paid June 12 trims Q3 invested assets by about 4%, so Q3 NII likely grows high single to low double digits year on year (Q3 2025: $41.3M). That supports underlying EPS of about $0.60-0.65 before development and cats.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: NII growth was cited in the Q2 2026 beat (+3.68%).
findings.why_not_priced: Largely in consensus already; filed as a small floor under the print rather than a surprise.
findings.independence: Same document as findings 4 and 5. Q3 2025 NII of $41.3M is in https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/84246/000110465925100820/rli-20251020xex99d1.htm.

findings.finding: A new buyback has room left: $250M authorized May 14, 2026, $238M of capacity remaining at June 30, and only $12M bought in Q2 at an average $51.25. Q3 buyback activity, disclosed in the release, could signal management's view of value after the stock traded $57-66 in Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None isolated. The Q2 print, with the authorization and $2 special dividend, got +3.68%.
findings.why_not_priced: Q3 repurchase volume is unknown until the release; the authorization itself is public.

findings.finding: Hurricane Isaias (Cat 2, landfall near Destin FL on Oct 9; industry insured loss $1-2B per Verisk, $3B per KCC, $2.5-4.5B per Moody's RMS) hits the Gulf/Florida Panhandle commercial-property footprint RLI names as a major cat exposure. It is a Q4 loss, but analysts are likely to ask for an estimate on the Oct 20 call, which falls inside the window.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None in the baseline. The Oct 2024 Beryl/Helene pre-announcement preceded a -3.06%... (that move was Jan 2026; the Q3 2024 print is outside the baseline window). Not established.
findings.why_not_priced: A mid-single-digit-billion industry event is small for RLI (likely under $15M net). The stock rallied 8% after landfall, which suggests the market has already shrugged it off, so it is sized small.

outside_window.finding: Isaias Q4 loss booked in the Q4 2026 print (January 2027); only commentary reaches the Oct 20 window.

searched_and_found_nothing: EDGAR 8-Ks 2026-07-23 to 2026-10-19: only the Jul 28 Reg FD exhibit and the Aug 13 regular $0.18 dividend 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/84246/000110465926095914/rli-20260813xex99d1.htm). No cat pre-announcement, no reserve 8-K.
Form 4s since July: routine RSU and option grants (director Bradshaw 2,153 RSUs on Aug 13; CEO Kliethermes 22,500 options at $61.29 on Aug 3). No open-market buys or sells.
RLI leadership news October 2026: nothing new (the last promotions were in April 2026, claims).
Option chain: unusable (no two-sided ATM quotes), so no implied move or skew.
No E&S peer (Kinsale, W.R. Berkley) has reported Q3 yet; Kinsale is due Oct 22, outside the window.
Search for the cause of the Oct 15-16 gap-ups found no RLI-specific news.

baseline_tension: The baseline has no option skew. My lean is up (a cat-light beat plus a crowded short), which agrees with the 8.4% five-day run-up and is therefore partly priced. That is why p_up is only 57 despite a likely ~25% EPS beat, and the run-up is the main reason the findings stay small.
lessons_applied: Lesson 5 (documents beat inference; weather reasoning has not paid): trimmed the Atlantic-quiet proxy from +1.0 to +0.8 and the no-pre-announcement inference from +0.6 to +0.5. Both stay filed.

Lesson 7 (check short interest before any negative; a crowded short shrinks negatives): SI is 9.6% of shares outstanding with 10.8 DTC, so Hawaii -0.8 became -0.7, property softening -0.6 became -0.5, casualty -0.4 became -0.3, the Travelers read -0.3 became -0.2, and Isaias -0.4 became -0.3.

Lesson 6 (verify the bar): two sources agree on ~$0.54 (MarketBeat $0.514, Earnings Whispers/Barchart $0.54), so no cap. The sweep's unsourced $0.58 was not used. Isaias's Q4 booking went to outside_window; only call commentary stays inside.

Lesson 1 (reaction function): RLI's beats were bought modestly (+2.78% on a 34% beat, +3.68% on a 15% beat) with one exception (-3.80%), so abs_move stays near the 3.65 median rather than scaling with the EPS beat.
